title: Acids, Alkalis and Indicators
seo_title: Secondary 2 Science: Acids, Alkalis and Indicators Worksheets with Answers
standard_code: Secondary 2: Chemical Changes (Acids, alkalis and indicators)
standard_text: Investigate the reactions between acids and alkalis, acids and metals, and acids and carbonates, and represent them with word equations; investigate the effect of acidic, alkaline and neutral solutions on litmus, Universal Indicator and natural indicators; recognise uses of neutralisation (summary of the MOE Lower Secondary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 2 science worksheets for Singapore students on acids and alkalis: pH, litmus, Universal Indicator, natural indicators, neutralisation and reactions with metals and carbonates. With answers.
key_big: Below pH 7 acidic, 7 neutral, above 7 alkaline.
body_html:
How to think about it

Indicators show whether a solution is acidic, neutral or alkaline.

  • pH scale: below 7 acidic, 7 neutral, above 7 alkaline. Universal Indicator: red (strong acid) → green (neutral) → purple (strong alkali).
  • Litmus: acids turn blue litmus red; alkalis turn red litmus blue. Natural indicators: red cabbage, butterfly pea flower.
  • acid + alkali → salt + water (neutralisation).
  • acid + metal → salt + hydrogen. acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide.
Example

A solution has pH 3. Acidic, neutral or alkaline?

Below 7

Answer: acidic

Example

zinc + hydrochloric acid → ?

acid + metal → salt + hydrogen

Answer: zinc chloride + hydrogen

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a high pH is strongly acidic. High pH is alkaline.
  • Mixing up litmus colours: acids turn blue litmus red.
  • Saying acids and metals give carbon dioxide. They give hydrogen.
  • Forgetting the salt: neutralisation gives a salt and water.

faq.a: Acids turn blue litmus red. Alkalis turn red litmus blue. Neutral solutions do not change either.

c: no gas; a salt and water form
